### Observed differences

- The clearest shift concerns A01's placement. In the earlier window A01 occurred early in each case (mean relative position about 0.26, median about 0.17); in the later window it occurs late (mean about 0.65, median about 0.67), while remaining present in essentially every trace in both windows. [POS001]

- The order between A01 and A02, A04, A05 and A07 reversed. Earlier, A01 preceded A05 in about 81 of 100 cases and A07 in about 68 of 100, and ran in mixed order against A02 (about 55/45) and A04 (about 49/51); in the later window A07 precedes A01 in all cases, A04 precedes A01 in all cases, A02 precedes A01 in about 81 of 100, and A05 precedes A01 in about 63 of 100. All five activities still co-occur in every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]

- Successor profiles changed accordingly. In the later window A01's outgoing transitions go mainly to A03 (about 47 in 100, up from about 7), while A04 and A07 are no longer observed as its direct successors (about 18 and 7 in 100 before); A07 now leads mainly to A01 (about 68 in 100, up from about 18) and no longer directly to A03 (about 28 in 100 before); A04 no longer leads directly to A01 (about 16 in 100 before); and A02 shifted away from A01 (about 26 to 11 in 100) toward A05 (about 27 to 40 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

- Step distances moved consistently with this reordering. A01→A03 is now typically adjacent (distance 1 in about 47 of 100 observed pairs versus about 10, with the earlier mass at distances 4–5 largely gone); A07→A01 within five steps appears in all 200 later traces (about 65 of 200 before), mostly adjacent; A04→A01 within five steps rose from about 103 to all 200 traces and A05→A01 from about 39 to 126, both now at longer distances; A02→A01 distances lengthened (adjacent in about 57 of 100 before, about 13 now); and the ordered pair A01→A05 fell from about 161 to 74 of 200 traces while its reverse rose. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007]

- Secondary shifts: A02, A05 and A07 each moved slightly earlier (mean relative positions down by roughly 0.08–0.10, medians from about 0.33 to 0.17). [POS002, POS003, POS004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 now runs at a much later point in the case, after the activities it used to precede. In the earlier window A01 sat early (mean relative position about 0.26) and mostly preceded A05 and A07, with mixed order against A02 and A04; in the later window it sits about two-thirds into the trace and runs after A07 and A04 in all cases, after A02 in about 81 of 100 and after A05 in about 63 of 100, with A03 now its dominant successor (about 47 of 100 of A01's outgoing transitions, up from about 7). The order reversals are shown directly for all four pairs, the successor profiles of A01, A02, A04 and A07 and the step-distance distributions all move in the same direction, and co-occurrence stays at 100% throughout, so this is a reordering of a fixed set of activities rather than a participation or path-replacement change. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, POS001, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007]

The volume of evidence also exceeds what an unchanged process typically produces: 21 control-flow items qualified where roughly 0.18 would be expected by chance across the 37 tested units, and each item's difference exceeds that seen in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits. The main limitation is mechanism: the reversed relative order and A01's later position are established, but the evidence cannot show whether A01 alone was repositioned or the block A02/A04/A05/A07 was regrouped earlier around it (A02, A05 and A07 also shifted slightly earlier). Positions are event positions within the trace, not clock times, so no conclusion about timing is possible. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]

Other differences: pairs not involving A01 show modest distance changes — A07→A03 lost its adjacent step (about 28 of 100 before, none now), and A07→A05 and A05→A03 shifted toward longer distances (A05→A03 at distance 5 rose from about 12 to 32 of 100). [LAG006, LAG008, LAG009]
